To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the long-term (2006–2015) variation trends of multiple pollutants in North China Plain were analyzed by using the multi-remote sensing satellite data.
the multi-year variations in AOD, NOx and SO2 over the NCP were mainly affected by the changes of biomass burning, vehicle exhaustions and industrial emissions.

(1) the minimum AOD values occurred in summer, and the minimum NO2 and SO 2 values occurred in summer and autumn, respectively; (2) the highly polluted regions were mainly distributed along the main line from Taiyuan-Lingyi; (3) AOD and SO 2 had declined since 2011 and NO2 had increased; and (4) the decline in SO2 was mainly attributed to the implementation of desulfurization devices.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the long-term variations and spatial distributions of AOD, NOx and SOx in the North China Plain, and provides references for future studies on the regional air quality and the corresponding control strategies.
the long-term variations of AOD, NOx and SO2 in the North China Plain, which can be used to provide scientific reference for the formulation of atmospheric environment management policies.
the spatial distribution and long-term variation of AOD, NOx and SO2, and provides scientific reference for the prevention and control of regional air pollution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the air pollution in North China has improved significantly in the last ten years, especially in SO2 and AOD.
AOD is mainly caused by dust, NO2 is mainly caused by vehicle exhaustions, and SO2 is mainly caused from coal combustion.
the air quality of North China Plain is still in a poor state, but it is improving.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AOD and SO 2 have a good linear relation, while the relationship between NO2 and other pollutants is not obvious, and the NO2 and SO 2 emissions are more sensitive to economic development.
the multi-remote sensing products are helpful for the analysis of the spatial distribution characteristics of the three polluted parameters and the evaluation of the emission control effects.
the control measures of AOD, NOx and SO2 are not the same.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, the multi-remote sensing products can be used to provide a comprehensive view of the spatial and temporal variations in the air quality, and can provide a scientific basis for the formulation of regional air quality control strategies.

the multi-remote sensing observations can be applied to provide a new perspective for the study of long-term atmospheric pollution and its sources, as well as to provide an effective method for the evaluation of the emission reduction effect.

the multi-remote sensing technology can provide an important basis for the evaluation of the air pollution control effect, and the remote sensing data are also an important supplement to the traditional ground monitoring data.
